title: What is an Agent?
description: Define the properties that distinguish an AI agent from a simple chatbot: autonomy, goal-directed behavior, tool use, planning, and memory.

data.text: What Makes an AI System an Agent?

Traditional AI assistants like chatbots are reactive: they wait for user input, then respond. An agent, by contrast, is proactive. It pursues goals, decides which actions to take, uses tools to affect the world, and learns from the results.

Agents exist on a spectrum. At one end are simple reflex agents that map percepts directly to actions (like a thermostat). At the other end are rational agents that maintain beliefs about the world, plan sequences of actions, and choose those expected to maximize their performance measure.

data.caption: Spectrum of agent types from simple reflex to learning agents

data.text: For software engineers, the most relevant agents are goal-based or utility-based LLMs augmented with tools (like web search, code execution, APIs) and memory. This combination enables behaviors like: breaking down a task into subtasks, browsing documentation, writing and testing code, and iterating based on feedback.

data.question: Consider a coding assistant that can edit files, run tests, and browse the web. Which agent type does it most closely resemble, and why?
data.answer: It resembles a goal-based agent: it has a goal (e.g., "fix the failing test"), formulates a plan (reproduce failure → hypothesize cause → edit → test → iterate), and uses tools (editor, test runner, browser) to achieve subgoals.
